messages.subject: acf plotting function for ggplot2
parts:
Dear all,

I have written a function to plot autocorrelation with ggplot2 similar
to the way the standard acf function does. Probably there´s some
niftier way to do it, but maybe it can help someone else, too.
Certainly the result looks better than the standard acf plot. If you
have any suggestions, hints, general advice - I am happy to learn it.

Here´s the function:

#### two supporting functions...
### the first support function is just to crop the result of acf in
order to get a result that can be processed easily by lapply and
as.data.frame

ret_acf =function(x){
a=acf(x,plot=FALSE,lag.max=length(x))
return(a$acf)
}

### this calculates the CI threshold the same like acf does.
calc_ci = function(ci,n){


a=c(qnorm((1 + 0.95)/2)/sqrt(n),qnorm((1 + 0.95)/2)/sqrt(n)*(-1))

return(a)


}


## this is a simple function that accepts dataframes containing one or
more timeseries and returns a facet grid plot of all the series in the
frame. plotting paramaters (alpha, color etc.) could also be added to
these arguments


ggplot_acf =function(dframe,ci){

r=lapply(dframe,"ret_acf")
r=as.data.frame(r)
r=cbind(1:dim(r)[1],r)
names(r)[1]="lag"

r=melt(r,id="lag")


q=qplot(lag,value,data=r,geom="bar",stat="identity",position="identity",ylab="acf",main="Autocorrelations")
+ facet_grid(variable~.) +geom_hline(yintercept=calc_ci(ci=ci,n=dim(r)
[1]),color="blue",size=0.1)
+geom_hline(yintercept=calc_ci(ci=ci,n=dim(r)
[1])*(-1),color="blue",size=0.1)
+geom_hline(yintercept=0,color="red",alpha=0.9,size=0.2)

return(q)

}

best

matt
